mainTopic: How Temple vessels, ירושלים and the עזרה are made holy: anointing versus service for vessels, the חמץ loaves of the תודה for the city, and שירי מנחה for the עזרה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a דרשה: "וכן תעשו" teaches that what was done in the משכן must also be done in later generations. רבא challenges this from a ברייתא. It says משה's vessels became holy through anointing (משיחה), but later vessels become holy through their first use in the service (עבודה). The גמרא answers that the word "אותם" limits anointing to משה's vessels. רב פפא brings the future-tense פסוק "אשר ישרתו" to show that later vessels depend on service. The גמרא then explains why both words are needed. Next, the גמרא turns to the משנה's "two תודות" used to add to ירושלים. A ברייתא and a פסוק in נחמיה show that this means the חמץ loaves, the largest part of the תודה. Finally, רמי בר חמא teaches that the עזרה is made holy with שירי מנחה, food that becomes unfit if it leaves the עזרה, just as the תודה loaves become unfit if they leave ירושלים.

steps.title: The phrase "and so shall you do" applies to later generations
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous teaching: the words "וכן תעשו" teach that the rules of the משכן apply to later generations too.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And so shall you do" means: in future generations as well.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a teaching that began just before this section. The extra words "וכן תעשו" teach that what was done in the משכן must also be done later on. It also sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already told משה to build the משכן according to the pattern he was shown, so "וכן תעשו" looks extra. The גמרא reads these extra words as a rule for the future (לדורות). The next steps will test how far this rule really goes.

keyTerms.meaning: For future generations; for all later times

phrases.english: "And so shall you do" – for future generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever was done for the משכן must also be done in later generations.

steps.title: רבא's challenge: later vessels don't need anointing
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. It says only משה's vessels were made holy by anointing, while later vessels become holy through use. That seems to contradict "וכן תעשו" לדורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: "All the vessels that משה made were made holy by being anointed. From then on, using them in the service makes them ready." Why? We should say "וכן תעשו" means later generations too, so later vessels should also need anointing!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the rule from step 1. If everything from the משכן carries over to later generations, why don't later vessels need anointing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly separates two time periods. משה's vessels became holy through משיחה, and later vessels through עבודה. If "וכן תעשו" really meant "copy everything," anointing should have carried over too.

keyTerms.meaning: Service; using the vessel in the Temple service
Inaugurates them; makes them ready for use

steps.confusionAlert: "Their service" means the vessel's first use in the Temple. That first use is what makes a later vessel holy. No anointing is needed for it.

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
All the vessels that Moses made –
their anointing makes them holy;
from here on –
phrases.notes: He means vessels made after משה's time, in later generations.

phrases.english: their service inaugurates them.
But why?
Let us say "and so shall you do" – for future generations!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that "וכן תעשו" carries everything from the משכן into later generations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says later vessels do not need anointing. That contradicts carrying over משה's method.

steps.title: A special verse limits anointing to משה's vessels
steps.stepSummary: Vessels are different, because the פסוק says "he anointed them". The word "them" means only משה's vessels needed anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says, "And he anointed them and consecrated them." "Them" were made holy by anointing, but later vessels are not made holy by anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא. Vessels are an exception, because a specific פסוק says anointing was only for משה's vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule of "וכן תעשו" still holds. Here, though, the word "אותם" (them) narrows anointing to that first set of vessels. A specific limit in the פסוק beats the general carry-over rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "Them": a limiting word that points only to those specific items

phrases.english: It is different there,
for the verse says:
"And he anointed them and consecrated them" –
them – through anointing,
but not future generations through anointing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special verse creates an exception to the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "וכן תעשו" should require anointing for later vessels too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "אותם" limits anointing to משה's vessels, so later vessels are an exception.

steps.title: Maybe later vessels can use either method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps "אותם" only means משה's vessels needed anointing specifically, while later vessels could become holy through either anointing or service.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: "them" must be through anointing, but in later generations it can be either through anointing or through service!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 3. The word "אותם" might not rule anointing out for later vessels. It might only mean that anointing is not required for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read "אותם". It could mean "only them through anointing," or "them must be anointed, while later vessels have a choice." The challenge points out that the פסוק alone doesn't tell us which reading is correct.

phrases.english: Say: "them" – through anointing,
future generations – either through anointing or through service!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 3 read the word "אותם".
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 3's reading that "אותם" removes anointing completely for later generations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "אותם" could just mean anointing is required only for משה's vessels, leaving later vessels free to use either method.

steps.title: רב פפא: later vessels depend on service
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a פסוק in the future tense, "with which they will serve." It shows that the Torah ties later vessels to service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The פסוק says, "with which they will serve in the holy place." The Torah made them depend on service.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge from step 4. He brings a different פסוק, which shows that later vessels become holy through being used in the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "they will serve" are future tense, so the פסוק speaks about vessels of later times. It links their holiness to שירות (service). This settles the question: for later generations, service is the way vessels are made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק made them depend on

steps.whatToRemember: משה's vessels became holy through anointing. Vessels made in later generations become holy through their first use in the service. "וכן תעשו" carries the משכן's rules forward, except where a פסוק says otherwise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a general rule ("וכן תעשו" לדורות) can have specific exceptions, each one based on its own פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The verse says:
"with which they will serve in the holy place,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 4:12. The key word is "will serve". It is future tense, pointing to vessels of later times.

phrases.english: the verse made them depend on service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 with a new פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional verse settles which reading is correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Later vessels might be made holy through either anointing or service.
steps.terutzMaskana: The future-tense פסוק ties later vessels to service, so service is what makes them holy.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In later generations, Temple vessels become holy through their first use in the service, not through anointing.

steps.title: Why do we need the word 'them'?
steps.stepSummary: Now that 'אשר ישרתו' teaches that later כלים become holy through עבודה, the word 'אותם' seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the Torah wrote 'with which they will serve', why do I need the word 'them'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the Torah needs the word 'אותם' at all, since רב פפא's פסוק already teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, 'אשר ישרתו' showed that later כלים become holy through עבודה. If so, 'אותם' seems to add nothing new. The גמרא assumes that every word in the Torah must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Why do I need it? (this word seems extra)

phrases.english: Now that the Merciful One has written 'with which they will serve',
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא's פסוק from the last step.

phrases.english: why do I need 'them'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 5's source to make Step 3's source look unnecessary
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: 'אשר ישרתו' already teaches that later כלים are made holy through service, so 'אותם' seems extra

steps.title: 'Them' rules out anointing for later vessels
steps.stepSummary: Without 'אותם', we would have required later כלים to get both משיחה and עבודה. 'אותם' teaches that later כלים need no משיחה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had not written 'them', I would have said that only משה's vessels became holy by anointing alone. Later vessels would need both anointing and service, because it says 'and so shall you do'. So the Torah limited it with 'them': only they were made holy by anointing, and later vessels are not made holy by anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'אותם' teaches something 'אשר ישרתו' does not. It removes משיחה completely for later כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אשר ישרתו' alone shows that later כלים need עבודה. Because of 'וכן תעשו', we might still think they also need משיחה. 'אותם' tells us משיחה belongs only to משה's כלים, so each word has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Later כלים become holy through עבודה alone. 'אשר ישרתו' teaches that עבודה is needed, and 'אותם' teaches that משיחה is not needed.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say later כלים are anointed and also used. It says that is what we WOULD have thought without 'אותם'. The conclusion is service only.

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had not written 'them',
I would have said: it is these that are made holy through anointing alone,
but for later generations, through anointing and service,
since it is written 'and so shall you do';
so the Merciful One limited it by writing 'them':
them, through anointing,
but not later generations through anointing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by giving 'אותם' its own job
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word teaches a separate point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Later כלים would need both משיחה and עבודה because of 'וכן תעשו'
steps.terutzMaskana: Later כלים need only עבודה. משיחה was only for משה's כלים.

steps.title: The two thanks-offerings means their bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'two תודות' and a ברייתא that says this means their לחם, not their meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and with two thanks-offerings.' A ברייתא taught: the two thanks-offerings mentioned there mean their bread, not their meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's words 'two תודות' and brings a ברייתא explaining that the ceremony uses the תודה's לחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה comes with loaves of לחם. The ברייתא tells us the 'two תודות' in the ceremony refers to these loaves, not the animal meat. This sets up the question of where this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks-offering, which comes with loaves of bread

phrases.english: 'And with two thanks-offerings.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which lists what is needed to add to the city or the עזרה.

phrases.english: It was taught: the two thanks-offerings that they mentioned
means with their bread, and not with their meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, moving to the next phrase of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two תודות of the ceremony refer to their לחם, not their meat

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule about the two תודות. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a פסוק behind the ברייתא's rule. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of Step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the two תודות

steps.title: רב חסדא's verse from נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings the פסוק in נחמיה about 'two large thanks-offerings' that went around the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: the verse says, 'And I placed two large thanks-offerings, and they went in procession to the right on top of the wall.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the source: the ceremony in נחמיה, where two 'large' תודות were carried around the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that two תודות were part of making the wall holy. The word 'גדולות' (large) becomes the key, and the גמרא examines it next.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: As the verse says:
'And I placed two large thanks-offerings,
and processions to the right, on top of the wall.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9's request for a source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in נחמיה about two large תודות on the wall

steps.title: What does 'large' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'large' means. It rejects the idea of a large species, because then the פסוק would just say 'oxen'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'large' mean? If you say it means literally from a large kind of animal, then let the verse just say 'oxen'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא examines the word 'גדולות' in the פסוק and rejects the first possible meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'large' meant big animals like cattle instead of sheep, the פסוק could have simply said 'פרים'. Since it did not, 'large' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: What does 'large' mean?
If we say it means literally from a large species,
let it say 'oxen'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at a word in Step 10's פסוק

steps.title: Large for their kind
steps.stepSummary: 'Large' means the biggest animals of their own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means large within their kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'גדולות' means animals that are big compared to others of the same kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a bigger species, the פסוק means choosing the biggest and best animals within the species. This answer is challenged right away in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, large within their kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new meaning after Step 11 rejected the first one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The biggest animals of their own kind

steps.title: Does size matter before Heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 12. A teaching says big and small offerings are equally pleasing, as long as the person's heart is directed to Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does importance matter before Heaven? But a teaching says: about an animal burnt-offering it says 'a fire-offering, a pleasing aroma'; about a bird burnt-offering it says 'a fire-offering, a pleasing aroma'; about a meal-offering it says 'a fire-offering, a pleasing aroma'. This teaches that one who brings a lot and one who brings a little are the same, as long as he directs his heart to his Father in Heaven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the תודות were 'large of their kind'. Why would size matter to ה׳?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'אשה ריח ניחוח', are used for an expensive animal, a cheaper bird and a simple flour מנחה. This shows that the size of an offering does not make it more pleasing. What matters is the person's intention. So 'large of their kind' seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives a lot and one who gives a little

steps.whyThisMatters: This famous teaching says the value of an offering depends on the heart behind it, not on its cost or size.

phrases.english: Is there such a thing as importance before Heaven?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: נֶאֱמַר בְּעוֹלַת בְּהֵמָה ״אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״,
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: It says about an animal burnt-offering, 'a fire-offering, a pleasing aroma',
about a bird burnt-offering, 'a fire-offering, a pleasing aroma',
and about a meal-offering, 'a fire-offering, a pleasing aroma';
this teaches that one who brings much and one who brings little are the same,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ לְאָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם!
phrases.english: as long as he directs his heart to his Father in Heaven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 12's meaning of 'large'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching shows that size does not matter before Heaven, so choosing the biggest animals of their kind would have no purpose

steps.title: Large means the biggest part of the thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: 'Large thanks-offerings' means the larger part inside the תודה, which is the חמץ loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'large' means the large part within the תודה. What is that? The חמץ loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 13 with a new reading of the word 'large' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that the size of the animal cannot matter, since big and small offerings are equally pleasing. So 'large' cannot describe the animal at all. It describes the biggest portion of the loaves that come with a תודה, which is the חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: the large part within the thanks-offering

steps.confusionAlert: 'Large' here is not about a big animal any more. It points to the largest group of loaves that come with the תודה.

phrases.english: Rather, the large part within the thanks-offering,
and what is that? The leavened loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by reading 'large' in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word 'large' in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Large' meant the biggest animals of their kind.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Large' means the largest part of the תודה loaves, the חמץ.

steps.title: Proof from the measurements of the thanks-offering loaves
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that the חמץ loaves are the largest part of the תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the תודה came from five Jerusalem סאה, which are six wilderness סאה, which are two איפות. An איפה is three סאה, so that makes twenty עשרונים (tenth-measures): ten for the חמץ and ten for the מצה. The מצה had three kinds: loaves, wafers, and flour mixed with hot water and oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that the חמץ really is the biggest part of the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half the flour, ten tenth-measures, goes to the חמץ. The other half goes to the מצה, but it is split three ways. So the חמץ portion is three times bigger than any single kind of מצה, which is why it is called 'the large part.'

keyTerms.meaning: a measure equal to three סאה
loaves, wafers, and flour mixed with hot water and oil: the three kinds of מצה

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
The thanks-offering would come
from five Jerusalem se'ah of flour,
which are six wilderness se'ah,
phrases.notes: The סאה used in the wilderness was smaller than the later Jerusalem סאה.

phrases.english: which are two ephahs;
and an ephah is three se'ah,
so twenty tenth-measures:
ten for the leavened loaves and ten for the matzah.
And the matzah came in three kinds:
loaves, wafers, and flour mixed with hot water and oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 14 with numbers from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the חמץ is the 'large' part of the תודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מנחות about the flour measurements of the תודה.
steps.whatToRemember: In נחמיה, 'large thanks-offerings' means the חמץ loaves, the biggest part of the תודה. Those loaves were used to make the city holy.

steps.title: The Temple courtyard is made holy only with leftover meal-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rules that an addition to the עזרה is made holy with שירי מנחה, compared to how ירושלים is made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: The עזרה is made holy only with the leftovers of a מנחה. Why? It is like ירושלים. Just as ירושלים is made holy with something eaten in it, so too the עזרה is made holy with something eaten in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רמי בר חמא says which offering is used to make the עזרה holy, and gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושלים is made holy with תודה loaves, which are eaten in the city. So רמי בר חמא reasons that the עזרה should be made holy with food eaten in the עזרה. That food is the שירי מנחה, the part of a מנחה left for the כהנים to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: the leftovers of a meal-offering, eaten by כהנים

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
The Temple courtyard is not made holy
except with the leftovers of a meal-offering.
phrases.notes: This is what's left after a handful is burned on the altar. The כהנים eat it.

phrases.english: What is the reason? It is like Jerusalem;

phrases.aramaic: מָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם – דָּבָר הַנֶּאֱכָל בָּהּ מְקַדְּשָׁהּ,
phrases.english: just as with Jerusalem, something eaten in it makes it holy,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֲזָרָה – דָּבָר הַנֶּאֱכָל בָּהּ מְקַדְּשָׁהּ.
phrases.english: so too with the courtyard, something eaten in it makes it holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ירושלים ceremony and extends it to the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An addition to the עזרה is made holy only with שירי מנחה, by comparison to ירושלים.

steps.title: But thanks-offering loaves are also eaten in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The comparison does not work as stated, since תודה loaves are eaten in the עזרה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that the תודה loaves are not eaten in the עזרה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason רמי בר חמא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'something eaten in it' does not pick out the שירי מנחה. תודה loaves can also be eaten inside the עזרה. So by that reasoning, תודה loaves could make the עזרה holy too.

phrases.english: Is that to say that the thanks-offering loaves
are not eaten in the courtyard?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'something eaten in it' from Step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תודה loaves are also eaten in the עזרה, so this reason does not single out שירי מנחה.

steps.title: Food eaten only there, and unfit if taken out
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is sharpened: each place is made holy with food that becomes unfit if it leaves that place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like ירושלים. Just as ירושלים is made holy with something eaten in it that becomes unfit if it leaves, so too the עזרה is made holy with something eaten in it that becomes unfit if it leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the comparison by adding a second condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is food that is limited to that place, not just food that may be eaten there. תודה loaves become unfit only if they leave ירושלים, so they match the city. שירי מנחה become unfit if they leave the עזרה, so only they match the עזרה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like Jerusalem:
just as Jerusalem is made holy with something eaten in it
which, if it goes out of it, becomes unfit,
so too the courtyard is made holy with something eaten in it
which, if it goes out of it, becomes unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by making the comparison more exact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any food eaten in a place could make that place holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only food limited to that place, which becomes unfit outside it, makes the place holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why רמי בר חמא's rule picks out שירי מנחה in particular: they are the food tied to the עזרה.

steps.title: Should the meal-offering then be leavened too?
steps.stepSummary: If the עזרה is learned from ירושלים, maybe the offering used should also be חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there it is חמץ, should it be חמץ here too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further and asks if it brings an odd result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ירושלים, the loaves used were the חמץ ones. If the עזרה copies ירושלים in every detail, the שירי מנחה used for the עזרה should also be חמץ.

phrases.english: If so, just as there it is leavened,
phrases.notes: 'There' means ירושלים, made holy with the חמץ loaves of the תודה.

phrases.english: should it be leavened here too?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of Step 18 by carrying it one detail further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the עזרה to ירושלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, the חמץ detail should carry over to the עזרה as well.

steps.title: There is no such thing as a leavened meal-offering
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected, because a מנחה can never be חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think that? Is there such a thing as a חמץ מנחה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brushes off the challenge from Step 19 as impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה is always מצה, so the חמץ detail cannot carry over to the עזרה. The comparison only concerns food tied to its place, not whether it is חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: and can you understand it that way?

steps.whatToRemember: ירושלים is made holy with חמץ תודה loaves. The עזרה is made holy with שירי מנחה. Each is food that becomes unfit if it leaves its place, and the חמץ detail does not carry over.

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?
Is there such a thing as a leavened meal-offering?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the עזרה needs a חמץ offering.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A מנחה can never be חמץ, so the demand is impossible.
